[{"Name":"Glenn Rhea","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocIX6qjJ9smrbEbThr4DRnFLjdrGZA5-OJvqhdZq-fEV1WHvIg=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"I brought my vehicle to this shop based on the owner’s initial claim that he specializes in European cars. I own a Maserati, so that assurance was a key factor in my decision. I paid $100 for what was described as a diagnostic. After the diagnostic was completed, I was not provided with any written report, paperwork, scan results, or documented findings—only verbal statements.

This was not an isolated issue. The owner also ran a diagnostic on my partner’s vehicle and likewise did not provide any documentation or written results. He additionally stated he would obtain pricing for suspension-related repairs on that vehicle but failed to do so in a timely manner. When asked about the delay, his explanation was that he “forgot” and that it was the holidays—an explanation that is difficult to accept when customers are waiting on information they were promised.

After my diagnostic, the owner was unable to provide pricing for any of the parts he claimed were needed. There was no parts list, no labor estimate, and no clear outline of next steps. Despite presenting himself as experienced with European vehicles, he could not provide even a rough cost range. This made it unclear what value the diagnostic was intended to provide.

The owner also stated that he would feel “unethical” allowing me to continue driving the vehicle due to allegedly unsafe wheels, yet no repair plan, quote, or actionable solution was offered. No repair work was performed, and no services were rendered beyond verbal discussion.

Compounding the experience, the shop had relocated, and the new address had not been properly updated. As a result, we traveled unnecessarily and ended up at least two hours away from where we live, which added avoidable inconvenience and frustration.

Because there was no documentation, no pricing, and no tangible service outcome, I requested a refund. When I later messaged the owner requesting my money back and informing him that I would be posting a Google review to document my experience, he called me in an upset and defensive manner. During that call, his tone was rude, extremely unprofessional, and he hung up on me, which further reinforced my concerns about how customers are treated.

I expect transparency, follow-through, and basic professionalism when paying for diagnostics and automotive services. Unfortunately, this experience lacked clear communication, accountability, and respect. It is already difficult to find honest, reliable mechanics who stand behind their work and communicate clearly, and this experience did not meet those expectations. Well come to find out it was my my evaporator core that was in need of replacement,  which Cody figured out .  He told me it would take a couple of day to remove and replace .But those couple of days turned into a couple weeks. I needed my vehicle for a trip I had planned many months ago . He asked me if I wanted him to check it out and get it fixed .I told him no , he already had my vehicle for over 3 weeks and it my wife vehicle she uses to get to work . Also for these 3 week my wife and son are ubering to school and work .I get my vehicle back and  there are fingerprints all over the place.  I spend about 2hrs just cleaning everything , which im upset about.  Since having my car for as long as they did they could at least clean the interior.  As for the infotainment situation the screen brand new runs about 500 , so I buy a used one for about 80 . I remove and replace the screen and have the same issue. After doing some research I  decided to check the connection to the radio receiver and found out the the connector that the screen recieves it's  input wasnt plugged in alll the way.  I push the connector in all the way and the infotainment screen works as intended with my reverse camera working as well . I fixed the problem they created which shouldnt have been an issue to begin with. Im upset with the auto clinic with how dirty they left my vehicle with fingerprints on all the panels, seats and windows. To having extra time with my vehicle and creating a problem with my infotainment screen to where they assured me everything was connected properly which it wasnt . To the lack of communication because I had to call them every time I wanted an update. Yes he did fix my air conditioning,  but created another issue. Im just stating what my experience was and hope it helps other people on deciding if they want to take there vehicle here. Affordable and reliable, highly recommend.","Images":null,"When":""},{"Name":"Thomas","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjUUDXoTjJExEAmHGECwVVGB1Nu8oWCI_9ftNbK3sFJZpWF2GDV8=s120-c-rp-mo-ba2-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"EDIT: I have changed no words, all I've changed is the star from 2 to 1 after the condescending reply from the shop.

I brought in my Grand Marquis in an emergency situation, I needed an intake manifold put on fast.  As I was on my way to California from Houston.  I was treated well and made comfortable with anything I had wanted to talk about.

However, I was unfortunately misled twice and have had issues with the replaced parts just days after they were done.

I was given a lower price overall because I was in a budget pinch, and I was told "AutoZone gave us the part cheaper" when the reality was they were just using a more cost effective part.  That would've been fine if that's how it was presented to me because in the situation the brand of the intake manifold on these cars is very important and unfortunately the one they went with is one I've known to have issues and in my thankfulness and gratitude I was feeling for the speedy repair, I lost sight of the details and didn't find out the part number until my cooling system blew up in Arizona.

The next disappointment is I was comforted by a "nationwide warranty" which would have solved this entire problem, because in theory a warranty you get told is for your repair actually covers the repair the shop did.  Well guess what, folks?  The warranty doesn't cover "internal engine components".   I can go back and forth with you as to why an intake manifold isn't internal, but that's neither here nor there, because I'm not the warranty adjuster and I don't make the rules.

So, I'm sure they aren't bad people, but I had a bad experience.
